questions.question: A crayon is 8 cm long. A pencil is 15 cm long. Which is longer?
questions.explain: 15 is bigger than 8, so the pencil is longer. When both are in cm you just compare the numbers.

questions.question: Three sticks: 5 cm, 20 cm, and 10 cm. Which is the shortest?
questions.explain: 5 is the smallest number, so the 5 cm stick is the shortest. Compare the numbers when they all use the same unit.

questions.question: A door is 2 m tall. A cat is 20 cm tall. Which is taller?
questions.explain: 2 m is 200 cm, which is much bigger than 20 cm, so the door is taller. Change to the same unit before you compare.

questions.question: A table is 60 cm wide. A book is 25 cm wide. Which is wider?
questions.explain: 60 is bigger than 25, so the table is wider. You can compare them right away because they are both in cm.

questions.question: Mia's arm is 30 cm long. The kitchen table is 75 cm long. How many cm longer is the table?
questions.explain: Subtract: 75 minus 30 is 45. A common trap is adding them to get 105, but the question asks how many more.

questions.question: Sam's jump is 1 m. Lily's jump is 60 cm. Who jumped farther?
questions.explain: 1 m is 100 cm, which is more than 60 cm, so Sam jumped farther. Don't just compare 1 and 60; the units matter.

questions.question: Three books on a shelf: Book A is 15 cm wide, Book B is 30 cm wide, Book C is 20 cm wide. Which is the widest?
questions.explain: 30 is the biggest number, so Book B is the widest. Just find the largest number when they are all in cm.

questions.question: A snake is 1 m long. A garden hose is 80 cm long. Which is longer?
questions.explain: 1 m is 100 cm, which is more than 80 cm, so the snake is longer. Compare 100 and 80, not 1 and 80.

questions.question: A pencil is 15 cm long. A pen is 23 cm long. How many cm longer is the pen?
questions.explain: 23 minus 15 is 8 cm. Adding them gives 38, but the question asks how many cm longer, so subtract.

questions.question: A ribbon is 40 cm long. A string is 1 m long. How many cm longer is the string?
questions.explain: 1 m is 100 cm, so 100 minus 40 is 60 cm. A common trap is adding 40 and 100 to get 140.

questions.question: Tom says, '90 cm is longer than 2 m, because 90 is bigger than 2.' What went wrong?
options: He added the two numbers instead of comparing
He read 2 metres as 2 centimetres by mistake
He compared the numbers but ignored the units
He swapped 90 and 2 and got the order wrong
questions.explain: Tom compared 90 and 2 without looking at the units. 2 m is really 200 cm, so 90 cm is shorter, not longer.

questions.question: A desk is 70 cm wide. A shelf is 1 m wide. How many cm wider is the shelf?
questions.explain: 1 m is 100 cm, so 100 minus 70 is 30 cm. Adding them gives 170, but we need the difference, not the sum.
